liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **They Love Each Other** (2 reviews): They Love Each Other was a scorcher early in the show; They Love Each Other also stood out for this attendee [15][17]
- **Ramble on Rose** (2 reviews): Ramble on Rose was played at a very rocking tempo; Jerry's lead in Ramble on Rose carried the crowd along through round after round [13][14]
- **Attics of My Life** (2 reviews): Second set ends tightly with Attics of My Life flowing into Not Fade Away; Attics of My Life is singled out as a highlight [8][10]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Jack Straw opener was scorching, with Jerry nailing his lyrics [13]
- **Black-Throated Wind** (1 review): Black-Throated Wind was a real treat in the first set [15]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Bertha was a great closer for the first set [8]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): China Cat Sunflower into I Know You Rider stood out [17]

## Setlist highlights

- **Red Rooster**: back after 316 archived shows (1526 days); rare: 12 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1993-09-10.112807.bk.schmit.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 159 min [1]
- **gd93-09-10.dsbd.miller.28782.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 155 min; rated 4.25/5 by 20 [4]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sound is described as excellent [14]
- **gd93-09-10.akg.gardner.5441.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 159 min; rated 4/5 by 7 [5]. Said about its sound: Audience recording judged excellent, with clear sound and lively crowd response captured well; Calls this among the best audience recordings available [9][10]
- **gd1993-09-10.140461.fob.Schoeps-MK41.miller.sirmick.flac1648**: source not stated; 20 songs; 158 min [2]

## Around the show

- Younger fans in the crowd were dancing all night [9]
- Phil's bass playing was heavy and prominent throughout the show [9]
- Attendee with about fifty shows behind them recalls Richfield Coliseum as having consistently excellent acoustics, with a very energetic crowd [10]
- Reviewer attended on their 22nd birthday; the whole crowd left satisfied [12]
- Richfield Coliseum was old, hot and stuffy, far from central Cleveland; it was the reviewer's girlfriend's first show [17]
- Reviewer rates this the strongest of the 1993 Richfield run, though wishing it came from a soundboard [8]
- Attended all three nights and considers the first night of the run the best, not this one [11]
- Ranks the second night, watched from front row center, as the weakest of the run [11]
- Describes the first night as rocking, the second as softer, and this third night as filling in what was missing [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1993-09-10.112807.bk.schmit.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Alan Schmit; source: Source: (stand/ORTF/110^/DFC/Section) B&K 4011s > Neumann BS48i-2 > Panasonic SV-255 > DAT(m); [1]
- **gd93-09-10.dsbd.miller.28782.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: flac16 SBD -> Master Dat (48k) [4]
- **gd93-09-10.akg.gardner.5441.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Tony Gardner; source: Audience: AKG 568's [5]
- **gd1993-09-10.140461.fob.Schoeps-MK41.miller.sirmick.flac1648**: transferred by Charlie Miller and SIRMick; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source: (FOB) Schoeps MK41 > Panasonic SV-255 > dat(48k); Transfer: dat > Sony PCM-R500 > Tascam DA-3000> wav 16/48; Lineage: wav > iZotope RX6… [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Richfield Coliseum](https://www.dead.net/archives/1993/clippings/backstage-pass-richfield-coliseum-1) [21]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Richfield Coliseum - September 10, 1993](https://www.dead.net/show/september-10-1993) [22]
